C0.quote: fully implements the majority rule for binary social decisions
C0.note: Design of voting mechanisms implementing majority rule for binary decisions.

C1.quote: Majority voting with Random checks subgame perfect implements the majority rule
C1.note: Main results are implementation results, i.e. characterisations of the equilibrium outcomes of designed mechanisms (SPE, Nash, sequential). SB is included because the analysis turns on incentives to vote truthfully.

C2.2.note: Inputs are single votes for one of two options (optionally abstention), Y/N confirmation announcements, ratify/verify announcements, and in Bloc formation also nominations of p agents.

C2.3.note: Preferences or types θ are defined separately from votes.

C2.4.quote: The purpose of this lottery is to give incentives to agents
C2.4.note: Votes v_i are notated separately from types θ, and the paper discusses agents voting insincerely.

C3.1.note: All results are equilibrium or implementation results in which votes may differ from preferences.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH (binary votes or messages), so the applicability condition is not met. The paper does mention vNM utility representations consistent with ordinal preferences, used for SD.

C5.1.note: Formal results concern implementation of the majority rule. Welfare or efficiency language ('inefficiencies', 'socially desirable') appears only in the introduction and conclusion.

VOT.note: Information is complete in Props 1, 3, 4 and 5. Under incomplete information (Props 2 and 6) agents have i.i.d. priors over types and observe votes, which would be PARTIAL.

DES.note: The authors design the mechanism, but no designer is modelled as an acting agent.
